sources.name: OGC API - Records - Part 1: Core
sources.role: catalog record core, collection, query, profile, filtering, sorting and autodiscovery contract
verified_facts: The Record Core requirements define a core metadata schema intended to make resources discoverable through catalogs.
The Records API supports catalog searches using logically connected predicates, including spatial and temporal predicates.
Catalog records can be represented in JSON/GeoJSON or HTML, and profile selection can request representation variations.
semantic_limits: A discoverable catalog record is metadata and does not prove that the referenced distribution was downloaded, complete or authoritative.
Spatial or temporal catalog predicates select records; they do not execute parcel containment or terrain sampling.
Autodiscovery, sorting, filtering and schema conformance must not create a parcel-height business row without source-byte and measurement receipts.

sources.name: OGC API - Common - Part 1: Core
sources.role: HTTP, URI, query-parameter, landing-page, conformance and API-definition contract
verified_facts: The standard defines reusable fundamental building blocks applicable across OGC Web API standards.
Implemented conformance classes are advertised through a /conformance resource associated with the API landing page.
The standard defines common HTTP and URI behavior, landing-page links and human- or machine-readable API documentation.
semantic_limits: An advertised conformance URI proves an implemented interface contract only after the relevant tests; it does not prove data truth or numeric accuracy.
A landing page or API definition describes access behavior and does not prove that any source bytes were fetched or processed.
HTTP success, JSON validity and predictable URI behavior must not substitute for exact geometry, CRS, vertical datum, units or execution provenance.

sources.name: OGC API - Features - Part 2: Coordinate Reference Systems by Reference
sources.role: supported CRS advertisement, requested response CRS, bbox CRS and content CRS declaration contract
verified_facts: The extension allows feature geometry properties to be presented in supported coordinate reference systems beyond the core defaults.
Each supported CRS is referenced by a URI and collections advertise the CRS identifiers they support.
The extension defines how clients request a response CRS, supply a bounding-box CRS and determine the CRS used in a response.
semantic_limits: A supported CRS URI does not prove that coordinates were transformed correctly or that axis order and units were interpreted correctly.
CRS84h ellipsoidal height must not be treated as EPSG:5701 or Ordnance Datum Newlyn without an explicit vertical transformation.
A bbox expressed in a supported CRS is a query envelope and is not the exact HMLR parcel polygon.

sources.name: OGC GeoSPARQL - A Geographic Query Language for RDF Data 1.1
sources.role: RDF feature/geometry vocabulary, geometry serialization, spatial relation and query-function contract
verified_facts: GeoSPARQL defines an RDF/OWL vocabulary for representing spatial information and SPARQL extension functions for geospatial queries.
It distinguishes features from geometry objects and supports geometry serializations with CRS identifiers.
It defines topological relation vocabularies and functions that can test spatial relationships between geometries.
semantic_limits: A GeoSPARQL relation result is only as reliable as the loaded geometries, CRS declarations and query implementation.
Feature-to-geometry links do not prove cadastral authority, source version, geometry completeness or vertical datum.
Topological conformance and query success do not calculate maximum-minus-minimum elevation inside a parcel.
